{"notes": "Visit 5 (left 7:45). Picture: no change. Chain is dark from the start through the back to about (23, 9.3) and through the belly and bottom tail to the dark domino near (27, 8.9). The whole pale tail, from about (27.4, 9.3) around to (26, 5.3), is still pale. The back-end gap at about (23.5, 9.4) is still open, and nobody mentioned it this visit. I can't tell who placed what, so no credit or blame for chain state until the final push.

Sofia: Looked closely at the right edge and correctly said the tail is still pale, with a jammed domino at the belly turn and the line ending just short. That matches the picture and corrects Omar's earlier overclaim, politely. At 7:15 she announced a connect from the bridge end into the lowest pale tail domino and asked others to keep their hands off. Clear, careful coordination. But the tail was still pale when I left, so her fix is unproven. Ask her whether it landed and whether she knows about the back-end gap.

Omar: Accepted the correction without defensiveness and stayed hands off at her spot, offering to connect if it isn't dark. Good teamwork. His earlier bridge claim was overstated, so he needs to verify before reporting. Ask him whether he's aware of the back-end join.

Hana: Spotted that the lowest pale tail domino sits off to the side and gave a fallback (connect from the bridge end). Offered to check it goes dark. Useful advice, but she is still hands-off. Ask privately how she's using her time.

Jack: Spoke this time. He stayed back to avoid collisions and offered to take the top of the tail. Considerate, but he has done nothing visible. Ask him privately why he isn't taking a job, such as the open back-end join."}
